description: A save button that owns its own state: a muted saving face with a spinning badge, then a green tick when the save lands, then back to idle.
interactionNotes: Clicking it, or pressing Enter or Space while it is focused, starts the save: the button becomes a muted, non-clickable surface, a badge with a spinner pops into its corner, and the label swaps word by word with a short blur. When the save resolves the badge turns green with a check and the label reads as saved; after `successMs` everything returns to idle. A rejected promise sends the button back to idle without a success flash. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the label and the badge change instantly.

props.onSave: Called when the button is pressed. Return a promise and the loading state lasts exactly until it settles; a rejection returns the button to idle.
props.loadingLabel: Label while the save is running.
props.loadingMs: How long the loading state lasts when `onSave` returns nothing.
props.successMs: How long the success state stays before the button returns to idle, milliseconds.
props.successColor: Badge color in the success state.
props.disabled: Dims the button and blocks input.
props.ariaLabel: Accessible name, for when you do not want the visible label alone to name the button.
props.className: Extra class for the root wrapper.
props.autoPreview: Site preview only — the button saves, shows the tick and repeats by itself. Leave it off in normal use; `onSave` never fires while it runs.

tips: Return a promise from `onSave` and the loading state lasts exactly as long as the request; the built-in timer is only a stand-in for prototypes.
A rejected promise drops the button back to idle without a success flash. Show the error yourself from inside `onSave`.
The labels animate word by word, never letter by letter: splitting Persian letters across elements breaks their joining.
Colors default to the neutral dark pill; `backgroundColor` and `textColor` accept any CSS color, a theme variable included.
The badge sits on the inline-end corner and its ring separates it from the page, so keep the badge inside the root wrapper when you restyle it.
